questions.q: What question did the Pharisees ask Jesus in order to test him?
questions.a: The Pharisees asked Jesus if it was lawful for a husband to divorce his wife.

questions.q: What commandment had Moses given the Jews concerning divorce?
questions.a: Moses had allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce and then send his wife away.

questions.q: Why had Moses given the Jews this commandment concerning divorce?
questions.a: Moses had given this commandment to the Jews because of their hard hearts.

questions.q: To what event in history did Jesus refer when telling the Pharisees about God’s original design for marriage?
questions.a: Jesus referred to the creation of male and female at the beginning when telling about God’s original design for marriage.

questions.q: What did Jesus say the two people, the man and his wife, become when they are married?
questions.a: Jesus said that the two become one flesh.

questions.q: What did Jesus say about what God joins together in marriage?
questions.a: Jesus said that what God joins together, let no man tear apart.

questions.q: What was Jesus’ reaction when the disciples rebuked those bringing little children to him?
questions.a: Jesus was angry with the disciples and told them to permit the little children to come to him.

questions.q: How did Jesus say the kingdom of God must be received in order to enter it?
questions.a: Jesus said the kingdom of God must be received as a little child in order to enter it.

questions.q: What did Jesus first tell the man he must do to inherit eternal life?
questions.a: Jesus told the man he must not kill, not commit adultery, not steal, not testify falsely, not defraud, and must honor his father and mother.

questions.q: What additional commandment did Jesus then give the man?
questions.a: Jesus then commanded the man to sell at that he had and to follow him.

questions.q: How did the man react when Jesus gave him this commandment, and why?
questions.a: The man was sorrowful and walked away, for he had many possessions.

questions.q: Who did Jesus say had great difficulty entering the kingdom of God?
questions.a: Jesus said that the rich had great difficulty entering the kingdom of God.

questions.q: How did Jesus say even a rich person could be saved?
questions.a: Jesus said that with people it is impossible, but with God all things are possible.

questions.q: What did Jesus say anyone would receive who had left house, family, and lands for Jesus’ sake?
questions.a: Jesus said they would receive a hundred times as much in this world, with persecutions, and eternal life in the world to come.

questions.q: On what road were Jesus and the disciples traveling?
questions.a: Jesus and the disciples were traveling on the road going up to Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to him in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Jesus told his disciples that he would be condemned to death and delivered over to the Gentiles.

questions.q: What request did James and John make to Jesus?
questions.a: James and John requested to sit on Jesus’ right and left hand with him in glory.

questions.q: What did Jesus say that James and John would endure?
questions.a: Jesus said that James and John would endure the cup Jesus would drink, and the baptism with which Jesus would be baptized.

questions.q: Did Jesus grant the request of James and John?
questions.a: No. Jesus said that the seats at his right and left hand were not his to give.

questions.q: How did Jesus say the rulers of the Gentiles treat their subjects?
questions.a: Jesus said that the rulers of the Gentiles dominate their subjects.

questions.q: How did Jesus say those who wish to be great among the disciples must live?
questions.a: Jesus said those who wish to be great among the disciples must be servant of all.

questions.q: What did the blind man Bartimaeus do when many rebuked him, telling him to be quiet?
questions.a: Bartimaeus cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

questions.q: What did Jesus say had healed Bartimaeus of his blindness?
questions.a: Jesus said that Bartimaeus’ faith had healed him.

commentary.text: Christ's discourse with the rich young man.

Verses 1–12 Wherever Jesus was, the people flocked after him in crowds, and he taught them. Preaching was Christ's constant practice. He here shows that the reason why Moses' law allowed divorce, was such that they ought not to use the permission; it was only for the hardness of their hearts. God himself joined man and wife together; he has fitted them to be comforts and helps for each other. The bond which God has tied, is not to be lightly untied. Let those who are for putting away their wives consider what would become of themselves, if God should deal with them in like manner.

Some parents or nurses brought little children to Christ, that he should touch them, in token of his blessing them. It does not appear that they needed bodily cures, nor were they capable of being taught: but those who had the care of them believed that Christ's blessing would do their souls good; therefore they brought them to him. Jesus ordered that they should be brought to him, and that nothing should be said or done to hinder it. Children should be directed to the Saviour as soon as they are able to understand his words. Also, we must receive the kingdom of God as little children; we must stand affected to Christ and his grace, as little children to their parents, nurses, and teachers.

This young ruler showed great earnestness. He asked what he should do now, that he might be happy for ever. Most ask for good to be had in this world; any good, Ps 4:6; he asks for good to be done in this world, in order to enjoy the greatest good in the other world. Christ encouraged this address by assisting his faith, and by directing his practice. But here is a sorrowful parting between Jesus and this young man. He asks Christ what he shall do more than he has done, to obtain eternal life; and Christ puts it to him, whether he has indeed that firm belief of, and that high value for eternal life which he seems to have. Is he willing to bear a present cross, in expectation of future crown? The young man was sorry he could not be a follower of Christ upon easier terms; that he could not lay hold on eternal life, and keep hold of his worldly possessions too. He went away grieved. See Mt 6:24, Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

Christ took this occasion to speak to his disciples about the difficulty of the salvation of those who have abundance of this world. Those who thus eagerly seek the wealth of the world, will never rightly prize Christ and his grace. Also, as to the greatness of the salvation of those who have but little of this world, and leave it for Christ. The greatest trial of a good man's constancy is, when love to Jesus calls him to give up love to friends and relatives. Even when gainers by Christ, let them still expect to suffer for him, till they reach heaven. Let us learn contentment in a low state, and to watch against the love of riches in a high one. Let us pray to be enabled to part with all, if required, in Christ's service, and to use all we are allowed to keep in his service.

Christ's going on with his undertaking for the salvation of mankind, was, is, and will be, the wonder of all his disciples. Worldly honour is a glittering thing, with which the eyes of Christ's own disciples have many times been dazzled. Our care must be, that we may have wisdom and grace to know how to suffer with him; and we may trust him to provide what the degrees of our glory shall be. Christ shows them that dominion was generally abused in the world. If Jesus would gratify all our desires, it would soon appear that we desire fame or authority, and are unwilling to taste of his cup, or to have his baptism; and should often be ruined by having our prayers answered. But he loves us, and will only give his people what is good for them.

Bartimeus had heard of Jesus and his miracles, and learning that he was passing by, hoped to recover his eyesight. In coming to Christ for help and healing, we should look to him as the promised Messiah. The gracious calls Christ gives us to come to him, encourage our hope, that if we come to him we shall have what we come for. Those who would come to Jesus, must cast away the garment of their own sufficiency, must free themselves from every weight, and the sin that, like long garments, most easily besets them, Heb 12:1. He begged that his eyes might be opened. It is very desirable to be able to earn our bread; and where God has given men limbs and senses, it is a shame, by foolishness and slothfulness, to make themselves, in effect, blind and lame. His eyes were opened. Thy faith has made thee whole: faith in Christ as the Son of David, and in his pity and power; not thy repeated words, but thy faith; Christ setting thy faith to work. Let sinners be exhorted to imitate blind Bartimeus. Where the gospel is preached, or the written words of truth circulated, Jesus is passing by, and this is the opportunity. It is not enough to come to Christ for spiritual healing, but, when we are healed, we must continue to follow him; that we may honour him, and receive instruction from him. Those who have spiritual eyesight, see that beauty in Christ which will draw them to run after him.
